entries.heading: Electromagnetic Accelerator
bullets: Designed and built a two-stage coil gun, solving the challenge of precisely timing sequential electromagnetic coils to efficiently accelerate a projectile.
Used ANSYS Maxwell 2D for electromagnetic field simulation and coil-timing optimization, Fusion 360 for mechanical design, 3D printing for fabrication, and Arduino for stage-control logic.
Achieved approximately 11 m/s across two stages with a 54.64 g projectile using four 400 V, 330 µF capacitors.

entries.heading: Coilgun Timing Simulator
bullets: Built a Python coilgun simulator coupling circuit dynamics and projectile motion via position-dependent inductance, using a custom 4th-order Runge-Kutta solver.
Validated against the analytical RLC solution; confirmed 4th-order convergence and energy conservation with a relative error of 6×10⁻¹⁴.

Automated 22 tests across 3 Python versions in GitHub Actions. The model predicts a 46.8% velocity loss to magnetic suckback and a projectile-placement change that could raise exit velocity by 37%, pending hardware testing.

entries.heading: Arduino Sensor & Control System
bullets: Built a real-time sensor monitoring system using an Arduino Uno R3, integrating an ultrasonic distance sensor and temperature/humidity sensor with an OLED display.
Developed C++ firmware to read sensors, update an OLED display, and handle errors.
Integrated digital sensor inputs and implemented I2C communication with the OLED display.

entries.heading: UCI Master of Engineering Capstone Project Assistant
bullets: Revised 3D CAD models in Fusion 360 for printable concrete structures.
Assisted with fabrication and preparation of concrete molds used for ASTM material strength testing.
Collaborated with 4 MoE student researchers during prototype development and testing.

entries.heading: American Rocketry Challenge
entries.where: R&D and Simulation Lead · Irvine, CA
bullets: Improved simulated flight accuracy by 23.2% through iterative OpenRocket analysis.
Collaborated with a 7-member engineering team to design and build a 25.6-inch competition rocket.
Completed two competition qualification flights, achieving an official score of 139.8 total.
